To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the statistical mechanical approach to generally covariant theories is well defined, that it is possible to formulate the first and second laws of thermodynamics, and that the thermodynamical parameters depend on the thermalizing interaction and not on the dynamics of the component systems.

(a) a generally covariant quantum theory with a vanishing constraint Hamiltonian may be studied with the methods of statistical mechanics, and (b) the thermodynamics of the theory is completely determined by the properties (i.e. the coupling strength and range) of the thermalizing interactions.

(i) the entropy is given by the logarithm of the number of microstates, (ii) the temperature is determined by the strength of the thermalizing coupling, (iii) the energy density is given by the energy of the thermalizing interactions and the energy of the components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the following issues: (i) the existence of a notion of entropy in general relativity, and (ii) the existence of an appropriate notion of temperature in general relativity.
the possibility of applying the fundamental ideas of statistical mechanics to generally-covariant quantum theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present approach is an attempt to extend the notion of thermodynamical equilibrium to the context of generally covariant theories.

the present analysis shows that it is possible to apply the fundamental principles of ordinary statistical physics to generally covariant systems, provided that the system has an appropriate structure and that the interaction with the environment is appropriately designed.
the Boltzmann-like statistical mechanics of generally covariat quantum theories is well defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermodynamical properties of generally covariant systems with vanishing Hamiltonian can be determined by the properties (e.g., the strength) of the thermalizing interactions, and are independent of any other property of the system.
we have developed a statistical mechanical approach for generally covariant quantum systems.

the statistical mechanics of quantum generally covariant systems can be formulated in a similar way as for ordinary systems, provided that one is willing to consider the thermalizing interaction as a part of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statistical mechanics is not necessarily based on the existence of a notion of Hamiltonian or energy.
statistical physics is a powerful and flexible tool that can be used to study the dynamics of quantum gravity.
the absence of energy is not necessarily an obstacle for the application of statistical mechanics.
